heuristic_name: Match Between System and Real World
short_description: Speak the user's language. Follow real-world conventions. Information appears in natural, logical order.

positive.definition: UI copy uses domain-appropriate plain language without unexplained jargon
positive.evidence_required: cite a passage and why it lands for the audience

positive.definition: Icons follow recognizable conventions (search lens, trash for delete, gear for settings)
positive.evidence_required: name the icon and its action

positive.definition: Information order matches how a user thinks about the task
positive.evidence_required: name the surface and the order

positive.definition: Tone fits the audience (formal for enterprise, warm for consumer, playful for entertainment)
positive.evidence_required: cite the copy and the inferred audience

positive.definition: Layout uses a real-world metaphor that aids comprehension (calendar grid, file folder)
positive.evidence_required: name the metaphor and where it appears

negative.definition: Domain or technical jargon appears without explanation in user-facing copy
negative.evidence_required: cite the term and where it appears

negative.definition: Error or status message reads as raw system output (codes, stack traces, API responses)
Icon-only control uses an unconventional symbol that requires guessing
negative.evidence_required: name the icon and the action it triggers

negative.definition: Information appears in an order that conflicts with how users would naturally think about the task
negative.evidence_required: name the surface and the misordered elements

negative.definition: Tone clashes with the audience or context (corporate stiffness on a consumer app, etc.)
negative.evidence_required: cite a passage and the inferred audience

critical_negative.definition: Critical user-facing surface is in machine-language only (raw JSON, untranslated locale, full stack trace)
